title: 454. Trigonometry & Periodic Models: Adding Sinusoids of Equal Frequency
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Find the amplitude of the sum of a sine and a cosine with equal coefficients.
questions.question: What is the amplitude of \(y=\sin x+\cos x\)?
questions.explanation: A sum \(a\sin x+b\cos x\) is a single sinusoid with amplitude \(\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\). Here \(\sqrt{1^2+1^2}=\sqrt{2}\approx 1.41\). The value \(2\) would require both terms to reach their maximum \(1\) at the same \(x\), which never happens because the sine and cosine are a quarter period apart.
questions.hint: Use \(R=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\); the two terms do not peak at the same time.

questions.concept: Amplitude with coefficients three and four
questions.learningObjective: Compute the amplitude of a combination of sine and cosine.
questions.question: What is the amplitude of \(y=3\sin x+4\cos x\)?
questions.explanation: The amplitude is \(\sqrt{3^2+4^2}=\sqrt{25}=5\). Adding the coefficients, \(3+4=7\), is incorrect because the two terms are out of phase and never attain their maxima together.
questions.hint: Combine the coefficients with the Pythagorean formula, not by simple addition.

questions.concept: Writing sine plus cosine as one sine
questions.learningObjective: Express a sum of a sine and a cosine as a single shifted sine.
questions.question: Which expression equals \(\sin x+\cos x\) for every real \(x\)?
questions.explanation: Expand: \(\sqrt{2}\sin\left(x+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\sqrt{2}\left(\sin x\cdot\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}+\cos x\cdot\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)=\sin x+\cos x\). The version with \(x-\frac{\pi}{4}\) expands to \(\sin x-\cos x\).
questions.hint: Expand each candidate with the sine sum or difference formula and compare coefficients.

questions.learningObjective: Express a sum with unequal coefficients as a single shifted sine.
questions.question: Which expression equals \(\sqrt{3}\sin x+\cos x\) for every real \(x\)?
questions.explanation: The amplitude is \(\sqrt{3+1}=2\). Expand: \(2\sin\left(x+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=2\left(\sin x\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\cos x\cdot\frac{1}{2}\right)=\sqrt{3}\sin x+\cos x\). The version with \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) expands to \(\sin x+\sqrt{3}\cos x\), with the coefficients exchanged.
questions.hint: The phase \(\varphi\) satisfies \(\cos\varphi=\frac{a}{R}\) and \(\sin\varphi=\frac{b}{R}\) for \(a\sin x+b\cos x\).

questions.learningObjective: Find the maximum value of a combination of sine and cosine.
questions.question: What is the maximum value of \(y=5\sin x+12\cos x\)?
questions.explanation: The expression equals \(R\sin(x+\varphi)\) with \(R=\sqrt{5^2+12^2}=13\). Since the sine has maximum \(1\), the maximum value of \(y\) is \(13\). The sum \(5+12=17\) would need \(\sin x=1\) and \(\cos x=1\) at the same \(x\), which is impossible.
questions.hint: Rewrite the expression as a single sinusoid and use its amplitude.

questions.concept: Sum of two sinusoids in antiphase
questions.learningObjective: Add two equal sinusoids whose phases differ by pi.
questions.question: What is \(4\sin t+4\sin(t+\pi)\) for every real \(t\)?
questions.explanation: Since \(\sin(t+\pi)=-\sin t\), the sum is \(4\sin t-4\sin t=0\). Two sinusoids of equal amplitude and frequency that are half a cycle apart cancel completely. The value \(8\sin t\) would be correct only if the two were in phase.

questions.learningObjective: Recognise that adding sinusoids of equal frequency does not change the frequency.
questions.question: The function \(y=\sin(3t)+\cos(3t)\) is a single sinusoid. What is its angular frequency?
questions.explanation: Both terms have angular frequency \(3\), and \(\sin(3t)+\cos(3t)=\sqrt{2}\sin\left(3t+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\). Adding sinusoids of the same frequency changes the amplitude and phase but keeps the frequency, so it is still \(3\). The frequencies are not added.
questions.hint: Combine the two terms into one sinusoid and read the coefficient of \(t\).

questions.learningObjective: Express a difference of a sine and a cosine as a single shifted sine.
questions.question: Which expression equals \(\sin x-\cos x\) for every real \(x\)?
questions.explanation: Expand: \(\sqrt{2}\sin\left(x-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\sqrt{2}\left(\sin x\cdot\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-\cos x\cdot\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)=\sin x-\cos x\). The version with \(x+\frac{\pi}{4}\) equals \(\sin x+\cos x\). A check at \(x=0\): the original expression is \(-1\), and \(\sqrt{2}\sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=-1\).

questions.concept: Amplitude of a sum with a phase difference
questions.learningObjective: Find the amplitude of the sum of two equal sinusoids with a given phase difference.
questions.question: What is the amplitude of \(y=3\sin t+3\sin\left(t+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\)?
questions.explanation: For two sinusoids of amplitudes \(A_1\) and \(A_2\) with phase difference \(\delta\), the resulting amplitude satisfies \(R^2=A_1^2+A_2^2+2A_1A_2\cos\delta\). Here \(R^2=9+9+2\cdot 9\cdot\frac{1}{2}=27\), so \(R=3\sqrt{3}\approx 5.20\). The value \(6\) would be correct only for a phase difference of \(0\).
questions.hint: Expand the second sine, collect the coefficients of \(\sin t\) and \(\cos t\), and combine them.

questions.concept: Range of a combination with a constant
questions.learningObjective: Find the range of a combination of sine and cosine with an added constant.
questions.question: What is the range of \(f(x)=\sin x+\sqrt{3}\cos x+1\)?
questions.explanation: The sum \(\sin x+\sqrt{3}\cos x\) is a single sinusoid with amplitude \(\sqrt{1+3}=2\), so it takes all values from \(-2\) to \(2\). Adding \(1\) gives the range \(-1\le f(x)\le 3\). The other interval assumes that \(\sin x\) and \(\sqrt{3}\cos x\) reach their extreme values \(\pm 1\) and \(\pm\sqrt{3}\) simultaneously, which they do not.
questions.hint: Combine the two trigonometric terms into one sinusoid first, then apply the vertical shift.
